propositions: Detached compaction sweep workers that die between snapshot-write/retire-rename and git commit leave the shared tracker tree dirty (untracked *.retired files and uncommitted deletions), which blocks subsequent reconverge merges and strands local ticket commits.

The fold operation performs snapshot-write, retire-rename (tracked source to *.retired), and git commit as separate non-atomic steps with no rollback, creating a crash window where tree mutations persist but the fold is incomplete.

A crashed/killed/interrupted sweep must recover to a clean tree with all folded events preserved: the next sweep entry must converge working tree status to porcelain-empty without losing ticket deltas.

Intent journal must be written before any mutation; if journal write fails, the fold refuses (exit 1) without mutating the store; recovery discrimination must distinguish landed folds (snapshot in HEAD, clear journal), abandoned folds (journal + uncommitted snapshot, revert), and superseded folds (snapshot gone from disk, clear journal) without misclassifying transient git failures as "snapshot absent".

Incomplete rollback (reverse-rename fails mid-recovery) must retain the uncommitted snapshot as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT for fsck repair rather than delete it and lose folded events; journal is still discarded so recovery never revisits fsck territory.

Transient git faults (index.lock, timeout) during recovery probes must not be treated as "snapshot absent" — tri-state probe returns INDETERMINATE and recovery defers (keeps journal) rather than reverting a possibly-landed fold.
